fixes.explanation: That's the number, friend. "In the four hundred and eightieth year after the Israelites had come out of the land of Egypt…" Solomon began to build (1 Kings 6:1). The writer counts all the way back to Egypt, so this building day is hanging on a long, long timeline. Four hundred and eighty years is a LOT of crumbs on the counter.

Close, but that's not the one the text gives. The Bible says the four hundred and eightieth year after Israel came out of Egypt (1 Kings 6:1). Four hundred and thirty shows up in Exodus 12:40 as the time the Israelites lived in Egypt, and I think that's why it sounds familiar. For this building, the count is 480.

Not quite, friend. The text says Solomon, Israel's king, began building in the fourth year of his reign (1 Kings 6:1). So the building started in year four, not year one. The month was Ziv, the second month, when the work started.

Right on the money. The foundation went down in Solomon's fourth year, and the temple was finished in the eleventh (1 Kings 6:37-38). The text sums it up: "So he built the temple in seven years." Count it out year by year if you like. I did, with my mustache.
